newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S SENDZIMIR STEEL MILL 1996 NET FALLS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S SENDZIMIR STEEL MILL 1996 NET FALLS.

text.p: Poland's state-owned steel mill Huta Tadeusza Sendzimira, which eyes privatisation next year, sees its 1996 net at 18-20 million zlotys, down from 100 million in 1995, the firm's general manager said on Monday.
Jerzy Knapik told a news conference the lower profits were caused by harsh winter and bad climate in steel industry.
"Prices grew nine percent instead of expected 16 percent and it was reflected by the net profit which is estimated at 18-20 million zlotys this year," he said.
He said the steel mill had sales of 2.9 billion zlotys in 1996.
He said the firm, which hoped to be privatised by the end of next year, would begin the proces by becoming a treasury-owned joint stock company by the end of the first quarter of 1997.
He said the company would later spin off three separate units, stakes in which would be offered to strategic, foreign, minority investors by the end of 1997.
Earlier the treasury ministry said talks on selling a minority stake in the firm were carried out with world's leading companies. Later the stakes could be extended to majority holdings.
Knapik also said the steel mill would sign by the end of the first quarter a cooperation agreement with Daewoo Motor on steel sheets for car bodies produced in Poland.
